description: The file types AutoCAD reads and writes beyond DXF: drawings, templates and standards files, published DWF/DWFx, backup/autosave/lock files, plot styles and plotter configurations, linetype, hatch, shape and font definitions, customization files, programming files (LSP, FAS, VLX, DCL, DVB, ARX/DBX/CRX), slides, sheet-set and publishing files, tool catalogs, profiles, layer states and other support files. What each contains, which command creates or uses it, and the pitfalls when scripting around them.

tools.name: .dwg drawing file
tools.description: AutoCAD's native binary drawing format. The first six bytes hold the format version code (AC1015 for 2000, AC1018 for 2004, AC1021 for 2007, AC1024 for 2010, AC1027 for 2013, AC1032 for 2018 and later), and a file saved by any release in a family has the same format. Files written by Autodesk applications are marked as TrustedDWG.
tools.usage:
OPEN / QSAVE / SAVEAS (Files of type: AutoCAD 2018 Drawing, 2013, 2010, 2007, 2004, 2000, R14...)
SAVEAS format default: Options > Open and Save > Save as

parameters.name: version header
parameters.description: Bytes 0-5, e.g. AC1032.

parameters.name: DWGCHECK
parameters.description: System variable controlling the warning shown when a drawing was last saved by non-Autodesk software.

parameters.name: thumbnail
parameters.description: Embedded preview image (THUMBSAVE / RASTERPREVIEW settings).

tools.notes: AutoCAD 2025 still writes the 2018 format, so it opens in releases back to 2018. Use SAVEAS or DWGCONVERT to down-save for older software. Reading DWG outside AutoCAD requires RealDWG (Autodesk) or ODA libraries.

tools.name: .dwt drawing template
tools.description: A drawing file used as the starting point for new drawings, carrying units, layers, styles, layouts, page setups, title blocks and system settings. NEW prompts for a template and QNEW uses the default template set in Options; acad.dwt (imperial) and acadiso.dwt (metric) ship with AutoCAD.
tools.usage:
SAVEAS > Files of type: AutoCAD Drawing Template (*.dwt)
NEW > choose template
Options > Files > Template Settings > Default Template File Name for QNEW

parameters.name: Template location
parameters.description: Options > Files > Template Settings > Drawing Template File Location (TemplateDwgPath in Preferences.Files).

parameters.name: measurement
parameters.description: A template's MEASUREMENT value selects acad.lin/acadiso.lin and acad.pat/acadiso.pat for new content.

tools.example:
; create a new drawing from a company template in a script
_.NEW
C:\CAD\Templates\ACME-A1.dwt
; COM: acad.Documents.Add(r"C:\CAD\Templates\ACME-A1.dwt")
tools.notes: When FILEDIA = 0, NEW prompts on the command line for the template name; '.' selects no template. Keep templates on a shared read-only location so every user starts from the same standards.

tools.name: .dws drawing standards file
tools.description: A DWG-format file that defines CAD standards: layers, dimension styles, linetypes and text styles. STANDARDS associates one or more DWS files with a drawing, CHECKSTANDARDS reports and fixes violations, and the Batch Standards Checker audits many drawings.
tools.usage:
SAVEAS > AutoCAD Drawing Standards (*.dws)
STANDARDS (associate) > CHECKSTANDARDS (check)

parameters.name: STANDARDSVIOLATION
parameters.description: Controls notification of standards violations while drawing.

parameters.name: plug-ins
parameters.description: Standard checks for layers, dimension styles, linetypes and text styles.

tools.example:
; in the drawing: associate the standards file, then check
STANDARDS    -> Add C:\CAD\Standards\ACME.dws
CHECKSTANDARDS
tools.notes: LAYTRANS can also use a DWS as the target layer set. DWS files are ordinary drawings, so they can be edited like DWG files and saved back as DWS.

tools.name: .dwf / .dwfx design web format
tools.description: Compressed, secure publishing formats for sharing drawings for viewing, markup and printing without the DWG. DWFx is based on Microsoft XPS. They are produced by PUBLISH, EXPORTDWF, EXPORTDWFX or plotting with the DWF6 ePlot / DWFx ePlot PC3 and can be attached back as underlays with DWFATTACH.
tools.usage:
EXPORTDWF / EXPORTDWFX / PUBLISH (Publish to: DWF, DWFx)
DWFATTACH to reference a DWF in a drawing
MARKUPIMPORT for markups

parameters.name: single-sheet / multi-sheet
parameters.description: Publish can create one file per sheet or one multi-sheet file.

parameters.name: 3D DWF
parameters.description: 3DDWF exports 3D models.

tools.example:
; script: export all layouts to one DWFx (-EXPORT asks for format, plot area, file name)
-EXPORT
_dwfX
_All
C:\Out\issue_set.dwfx
tools.notes: PDF has largely replaced DWF for external exchange; DWF remains useful for markup round-trips with Autodesk viewers.

tools.name: .dxb drawing interchange binary
tools.description: A simple binary vector format produced by plotting to the 'DXB File' plotter configuration and imported with DXBIN. Because the plotter flattens everything into lines, plotting to DXB and importing the result is a classic way to turn 3D views, text and hatches into plain 2D line work.
tools.usage:
PLOTTERMANAGER > Add-A-Plotter Wizard > Manufacturer: AutoCAD DXB File
PLOT to the DXB device > DXBIN to import

parameters.name: DXBIN
parameters.description: Command that imports a .dxb file into the current drawing.

tools.example:
1. Plot the view with the 'DXB File.pc3' device to C:\Temp\view.dxb
2. In a new drawing: DXBIN  C:\Temp\view.dxb
tools.notes: FLATTEN (Express Tools) and FLATSHOT are more direct alternatives for 3D-to-2D conversion. The ODA File Converter can also write DXB.

tools.name: .bak backup file
tools.description: Copy of the previous version of a drawing, written next to it with the same name and a .bak extension each time the drawing is saved, when ISAVEBAK is 1. Rename it to .dwg to recover the previously saved state.
tools.usage:
ISAVEBAK = 1 (create) / 0 (do not create)
rename plan.bak -> plan_recovered.dwg

parameters.name: ISAVEBAK
parameters.description: Enables backup creation (and slightly slows incremental saves).

parameters.name: MOVEBAK
parameters.description: Express Tool that redirects BAK files to another folder.

tools.example: copy "C:\Proj\A-101.bak" "C:\Proj\A-101_prev.dwg"
tools.notes: Only one generation is kept; the next save overwrites it. Vault/PDM systems often filter .bak files out.

tools.name: .sv$ automatic save file
tools.description: Temporary automatic-save file written at the interval set by SAVETIME into the folder given by SAVEFILEPATH, named after the drawing with a numeric suffix. It is deleted when the drawing closes normally, so a leftover .sv$ usually means AutoCAD crashed; rename it to .dwg to recover work.
tools.usage:
SAVETIME = minutes (0 disables)
SAVEFILEPATH = folder
rename A-101_1_1_5832.sv$ -> A-101_autosave.dwg

parameters.name: SAVETIME
parameters.description: Autosave interval in minutes; the timer counts only while the drawing is modified.

parameters.name: SAVEFILEPATH
parameters.description: Folder for autosave files (defaults to the Windows temp folder).

tools.example:
(getvar "SAVEFILEPATH")  ; where to look after a crash
(setvar "SAVETIME" 10)
tools.notes: DRAWINGRECOVERY lists recoverable files after a crash. Cleaning the temp folder deletes autosaves, so point SAVEFILEPATH somewhere persistent.

tools.name: .dwl / .dwl2 drawing lock files
tools.description: Small files created next to a drawing when it is opened for writing; they record who has the file open (user name, computer and time) and let other users see that it is in use. They are deleted when the drawing closes.
tools.usage: A-101.dwg -> A-101.dwl + A-101.dwl2 while open

parameters.name: .dwl
parameters.description: Plain text with user name, machine name and date.

parameters.name: .dwl2
parameters.description: XML with additional user and machine information.

tools.example: type "P:\Proj\A-101.dwl"   :: shows who has the drawing open
tools.notes: After a crash stale lock files may remain and make the drawing appear in use; delete them only after confirming nobody has the file open.

tools.name: .ctb color-dependent plot style table
tools.description: Plot style table with 255 styles mapped to the ACI colors, so an object's plotted appearance (pen color, lineweight, screening, linetype) depends on its color. Used by drawings whose PSTYLEMODE is color-dependent; monochrome.ctb is the most common.
tools.usage:
Page Setup / PLOT > Plot style table (pen assignments) > monochrome.ctb
STYLESMANAGER to open the Plot Styles folder

parameters.name: PSTYLEPOLICY
parameters.description: 1 = new drawings use color-dependent styles (CTB).

parameters.name: PSTYLEMODE
parameters.description: Read-only: 1 when the current drawing uses CTB.

parameters.name: CONVERTPSTYLES / CONVERTCTB
parameters.description: Convert a drawing or a table between CTB and STB.

tools.example:
; assign a CTB to the current layout from AutoLISP
(vla-put-StyleSheet (vla-get-ActiveLayout (vla-get-ActiveDocument (vlax-get-acad-object))) "monochrome.ctb")
tools.notes: The CTB must exist in the Plot Styles folder (PrinterStyleSheetPath) on every machine that plots, or the plot falls back to default styles.

tools.name: .stb named plot style table
tools.description: Plot style table of named styles that are assigned to layers or objects through the Plot Style property, independent of color. Used by drawings whose plot style mode is named (PSTYLEMODE = 0).
tools.usage:
PSTYLEPOLICY = 0 before creating a drawing
Layer Properties > Plot Style column
PLOTSTYLE to set the current plot style

parameters.name: Normal
parameters.description: Default named style that plots objects with their own properties.

parameters.name: DEFPLSTYLE / DEFLPLSTYLE
parameters.description: Default plot style for new objects and new layers.

tools.example:
; switch an existing drawing from CTB to STB
CONVERTPSTYLES
tools.notes: Mixing CTB-based and STB-based drawings in xrefs works, but each file plots with its own mode; standardise across a project.

tools.name: .pc3 plotter configuration file
tools.description: Stores a plotter or printer configuration: driver, port or output file, media sources, custom paper sizes, resolution and other device properties. Created with the Add-A-Plotter wizard in PLOTTERMANAGER and referenced by page setups by name, e.g. 'DWG To PDF.pc3'.
tools.usage:
PLOTTERMANAGER (Plotters folder) > Add-A-Plotter Wizard
Plotter Configuration Editor: double-click a .pc3

parameters.name: PrinterConfigPath
parameters.description: Folder searched for PC3 files (Options > Files > Printer Support File Path).

parameters.name: custom paper sizes
parameters.description: Stored in the PC3 or the associated PMP file.

tools.example:
; plot to PDF via a PC3 from a script (-PLOT detailed configuration)
_-PLOT
_Y

DWG To PDF.pc3
ISO full bleed A1 (841.00 x 594.00 MM)
...
tools.notes: Page setups store the PC3 name, not its contents; missing PC3 files on another machine cause 'plotter not found' fallbacks. Distribute PC3 and PMP files together.

tools.name: .pmp plot model parameter file
tools.description: Holds calibration and custom paper-size data for a PC3 plotter configuration, stored in the Plotters\PMP Files folder and linked from the PC3.
tools.usage: Plotter Configuration Editor > Device and Document Settings > Custom Paper Sizes / Plotter Calibration > Save PMP

parameters.name: custom paper sizes
parameters.description: User-defined media names and printable areas.

parameters.name: calibration
parameters.description: Length correction factors for the device.

tools.example: Copy both "Large Format.pc3" and "Large Format.pmp" to the new workstation's Plotters and PMP Files folders.
tools.notes: If the PMP is missing, custom sizes defined in it disappear from the page setup list.

tools.name: .lin linetype definition file
tools.description: Text file of linetype definitions. Each definition has a header line *NAME,description and a pattern line A,dash,gap,... where positive values are dashes, negative values gaps and 0 dots; complex linetypes embed text ["TEXT",STYLE,S=..,R=..,X=..,Y=..] or shapes [SHAPE,file.shx,...]. acad.lin (imperial) and acadiso.lin (metric) ship with AutoCAD.

parameters.name: A
parameters.description: Alignment field; the only supported value.

parameters.name: S / R / U / X / Y
parameters.description: Scale, relative rotation, upright rotation and offsets of embedded text or shapes.

tools.example:
(command "_.-LINETYPE" "_Load" "GAS_LINE" "C:/CAD/Support/acme.lin" "")
; .NET: db.LoadLineTypeFile("GAS_LINE", "acme.lin")
tools.notes: Linetype definitions are copied into the drawing when loaded; later edits to the .lin do not update drawings until reloaded. MKLTYPE (Express Tools) creates definitions from drawn geometry.

tools.name: .pat hatch pattern file
tools.description: Text file of hatch pattern definitions: a header *NAME,description followed by one line per pattern line family: angle, x-origin, y-origin, delta-x, delta-y [, dash, gap, ...]. acad.pat and acadiso.pat contain the standard patterns.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Direction of the line family in degrees.

parameters.name: x-origin,y-origin
parameters.description: Base point of the family.

parameters.name: delta-x,delta-y
parameters.description: Offset along the line (stagger) and spacing between parallel lines.

parameters.name: dash, gap
parameters.description: Positive dashes, negative gaps, 0 dots; omit for continuous lines.

tools.example:
; custom pattern stored as BRICK_MM.pat on the support path
(command "_.-HATCH" "_P" "BRICK_MM" 1 0 "_S" (entlast) "" "")
tools.notes: A custom pattern in its own file must have the file name equal to the pattern name, and the file must end with a newline. Place custom files on the support path so HATCH lists them under Custom.

tools.name: .shp / .shx shape and font files
tools.description: SHP is the text source of shape definitions (symbols and single-line fonts) and SHX its compiled form. AutoCAD SHX fonts such as txt.shx, romans.shx and simplex.shx are shape files, and big fonts (e.g. for Asian characters) use the same format. Complex linetypes can reference shapes.
tools.usage:
COMPILE (SHP -> SHX)
LOAD (load a shape file for the SHAPE command)
STYLE (use an SHX as a text font)

parameters.name: SHAPE
parameters.description: Command that inserts a shape from a loaded SHX.

parameters.name: FONTALT / FONTMAP
parameters.description: Substitute font and font-mapping file used when an SHX is missing.

tools.example:
COMPILE  C:\CAD\Support\acme_sym.shp   -> acme_sym.shx
LOAD     acme_sym.shx
SHAPE    VALVE  <point> 2.5 0
tools.notes: Missing SHX fonts are the most common cause of '?' characters and substitution prompts; ship custom SHX files with drawings (ETRANSMIT includes them). DUMPSHX converts SHX back to SHP.

tools.name: .cuix customization file
tools.description: Zip-packaged XML file holding the user interface definitions: ribbon tabs and panels, toolbars, menus, Quick Access Toolbar, keyboard shortcuts, double-click actions, quick properties, rollover tooltips and workspaces. acad.cuix is the main file; partial CUIx files add company or application UI; an enterprise CUIx can be shared read-only.
tools.usage:
CUI (editor) / CUILOAD / CUIUNLOAD / CUIEXPORT / CUIIMPORT
Options > Files > Customization Files > Main / Enterprise

parameters.name: partial CUIx
parameters.description: Loaded under the main file; contents appear alongside acad.cuix commands.

parameters.name: MENUNAME
parameters.description: Read-only variable with the main customization file path.

parameters.name: .mnl companion
parameters.description: A LISP file with the same base name is loaded automatically with the CUIx.

tools.example:
(command "_.CUILOAD" "C:/CAD/Support/ACME.cuix")
; or declare it in PackageContents.xml as a ComponentEntry with ModuleName="./Contents/ACME.cuix"
tools.notes: Do not edit acad.cuix for company tools; use a partial CUIx so product updates and resets do not wipe customizations. Legacy .mnu/.cui files are converted with CUI > Transfer.

tools.name: .mnl menu LISP file
tools.description: AutoLISP file that AutoCAD loads automatically whenever a customization file (CUIx) with the same base name is loaded. It holds the LISP functions used by that CUIx's macros, keeping menu code and UI together.
tools.usage: ACME.cuix + ACME.mnl in the same support folder -> ACME.mnl loads with the CUIx

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Found via the support file search path; subject to SECURELOAD trusted locations.

tools.example:
;; ACME.mnl
(defun c:ACMEREV () (load "acme_rev.lsp") (c:ACMEREV_MAIN))
(princ "\nACME menu utilities loaded.")
(princ)
tools.notes: Keep .mnl files small and use autoload to defer loading large code until a command is used.

tools.name: .lsp AutoLISP source file
tools.description: Plain-text AutoLISP source code loaded with (load), APPLOAD, drag-and-drop, the Startup Suite, acad.lsp/acaddoc.lsp or an autoloader bundle. Since AutoCAD 2021, source files may be UTF-8 (Unicode) when LISPSYS selects the Unicode-aware LISP engine.
tools.usage:
(load "tools.lsp")
APPLOAD > Load / Startup Suite

parameters.name: LISPSYS
parameters.description: 0 legacy MBCS engine with the Visual LISP IDE; 1 Unicode engine with the AutoLISP Extension for VS Code (default); 2 VS Code editing with MBCS behaviour for compatibility with pre-2021 releases. Restart AutoCAD after changing it.

parameters.name: SECURELOAD / TRUSTEDPATHS
parameters.description: Only files from trusted locations load silently.

tools.example:
; acaddoc.lsp - loads company tools into every drawing
(load "C:/CAD/Lisp/acme_tools.lsp" "\nacme_tools.lsp not found")
(princ)
tools.notes: Supported in AutoCAD LT 2024+ (with LT limitations) and in the AutoCAD web app (only .lsp). Use FAS or VLX to distribute compiled code.

tools.name: .fas compiled AutoLISP file
tools.description: Compiled form of a single AutoLISP source file produced by vlisp-compile or the Make Application wizard. It loads faster than source and hides the code from casual inspection, while being loaded exactly like an .lsp file.
tools.usage:
(vlisp-compile 'st "tools.lsp")  -> tools.fas
(load "tools.fas")  or  (load "tools") which prefers .vlx, then .fas, then .lsp

parameters.name: load order
parameters.description: (load "name") without an extension tries .vlx, then .fas, then .lsp and loads the first file found.

tools.example: (load "acme_tools")   ; loads acme_tools.vlx, else .fas, else .lsp
tools.notes: FAS files compiled with LISPSYS = 1 (Unicode format) cannot be loaded by AutoCAD 2020 and earlier; compile with LISPSYS 0 or 2 for older targets. Not supported in the AutoCAD web app.

tools.name: .vlx Visual LISP application
tools.description: Packaged Visual LISP application that bundles several compiled FAS modules and resources (DCL dialogs, text files) into one file, optionally with its own separate namespace. Built with MAKELISPAPP (Make Application wizard).
tools.usage:
MAKELISPAPP (Make Application wizard) -> app.prv (make file) + app.vlx
(load "app.vlx") / APPLOAD

parameters.name: separate namespace
parameters.description: Isolates the application's variables and functions; export functions with vl-doc-export.

parameters.name: resources
parameters.description: DCL and TXT files embedded and read with load_dialog / vl-get-resource.

tools.example:
; inside a separate-namespace VLX
(vl-doc-export 'c:ACMEREPORT)
(defun c:ACMEREPORT () (load_dialog "report.dcl") ...)
tools.notes: vl-list-loaded-vlx and vl-unload-vlx manage separate-namespace VLX applications. Not supported in the AutoCAD web app.

tools.name: .dcl dialog control language file
tools.description: Plain-text file of dialog-box definitions written in DCL and loaded with load_dialog. Predefined tiles and prototypes come from base.dcl (and acad.dcl), which every DCL file can use.
tools.usage:
mydlg : dialog { label = "..."; : edit_box { key = "k"; } ok_cancel; }
(load_dialog "mydlg.dcl")

parameters.name: base.dcl
parameters.description: Defines standard tiles such as ok_cancel, errtile and spacers; never edit it.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Files are found on the support path unless a full path is given.

tools.notes: Syntax errors are written to acad.dce and reported when the dialog loads. DCL works in AutoCAD for Windows and AutoCAD LT 2024+, not on Mac or web.

tools.name: .dvb VBA project file
tools.description: Visual Basic for Applications project containing modules, class modules and UserForms that automate AutoCAD through the ActiveX object model. VBA must be installed separately (VBA module download for the matching release).
tools.usage: VBAIDE / VBALOAD / VBAUNLOAD / VBAMAN / VBARUN / -VBARUN project.dvb!Module.Macro

parameters.name: acad.dvb
parameters.description: If found on the support path it is loaded automatically at startup; a macro named AcadStartup in it runs.

parameters.name: embedded projects
parameters.description: Legacy option to embed a project in a DWG (security risk; avoid).

tools.example:
-VBARUN
C:\CAD\VBA\tools.dvb!Module1.ExportAttributes
tools.notes: VBA 7.1 in 64-bit AutoCAD needs PtrSafe declarations for Windows API calls. Autodesk recommends .NET for new development; VBA is not available in AutoCAD LT or on Mac.

tools.name: .arx / .dbx / .crx ObjectARX modules
tools.description: Native C++ DLL modules built with the ObjectARX SDK: .arx applications run inside AutoCAD, .dbx object enablers contain custom object classes loadable by any RealDWG host, and .crx modules target the core (accoreconsole, Design Automation) without UI dependencies. They are binary-compatible only within one release family.
tools.usage:
ARX (Load/Unload) / APPLOAD / (arxload "acme.arx")
acad.rx lists modules loaded at startup
DEMANDLOAD controls loading of object enablers

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: R24 for 2021-2024, R25 for 2025-2026; rebuild for each family.

parameters.name: acad.rx
parameters.description: Text file listing ARX modules to load at startup.

tools.example: (if (not (member "acmetools.arx" (arx))) (arxload "C:/CAD/ARX/acmetools.arx"))
tools.notes: Without the matching enabler, custom objects show as proxy objects. Not loadable in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: .sld / .slb slide and slide library files
tools.description: An SLD is a vector snapshot of the current view created with MSLIDE and displayed with VSLIDE; an SLB is a library of slides built with the SLIDELIB utility. Slides are used as previews in DCL image tiles, image-tile menus and scripted presentations.
tools.usage:
MSLIDE  name.sld
VSLIDE  name   or  VSLIDE  library(name)
SLIDELIB.EXE library < list.txt

parameters.name: library(slide)
parameters.description: Syntax to reference a slide inside an SLB in VSLIDE and slide_image.

tools.example:
; script: build a slide per block for a DCL preview library
_.MSLIDE
C:\CAD\Slides\valve.sld
tools.notes: Slides contain only vectors of the displayed view (no fills beyond outlines, no raster); regenerate them if block graphics change.

tools.name: .dst sheet set data file
tools.description: The sheet set data file created by NEWSHEETSET and edited through the Sheet Set Manager. It stores the sheet list and subsets, sheet and set properties (used in fields), resource and view locations, callout blocks, label blocks, page setup overrides and publish settings.
tools.usage: NEWSHEETSET / OPENSHEETSET / SHEETSET (Sheet Set Manager)

parameters.name: custom properties
parameters.description: Sheet-set and sheet properties referenced by fields in title blocks.

parameters.name: locking
parameters.description: The DST is locked while edited; others see it as read-only.

tools.example:
; open a sheet set from a script
_.OPENSHEETSET
P:\Proj\2026-017\2026-017.dst
tools.notes: Keep the DST on the project share with the sheets; broken paths after moving projects are fixed by editing resource locations. The Sheet Set Object (SSO) COM API (AcSmComponents) automates it.

tools.name: .dsd drawing set description file
tools.description: INI-style text file saved from the PUBLISH dialog that lists the sheets (drawing and layout pairs) and publish options. -PUBLISH or PUBLISH with a DSD reproduces a publish job, which makes DSD files the standard way to batch-plot to PDF or DWF from scripts.
tools.usage:
PUBLISH > Save Sheet List (*.dsd)
-PUBLISH  C:\Jobs\issue.dsd

parameters.name: [DWF6Sheet:...] sections
parameters.description: One section per sheet with DWG path, Layout name, Setup and OriginalSheetPath.

parameters.name: [Target]
parameters.description: Output format type, output location and the multi-sheet setting.

tools.example:
; run a saved publish job unattended
(setvar "BACKGROUNDPLOT" 0)
(command "_.-PUBLISH" "C:/Jobs/issue.dsd")
tools.notes: DSD files contain absolute paths; generate them programmatically (or edit them) when drawings move. BACKGROUNDPLOT 0 makes publishing synchronous in scripts.

tools.name: .atc tool catalog file
tools.description: XML file describing a tool catalog for the Content Browser / tool palettes, listing tools (blocks, hatches, commands) with their properties and source files. Individual palettes are exported and imported as .xtp files through CUSTOMIZE.
tools.usage:
TOOLPALETTES > Customize Palettes (CUSTOMIZE) > Export/Import .xtp
Options > Files > Tool Palettes File Locations

parameters.name: *.atc
parameters.description: Catalog/palette definition XML.

parameters.name: *.xtp
parameters.description: Exported palette for sharing between users.

tools.example: Options > Files > Tool Palettes File Locations: add P:\CAD\Palettes (shared, read-only for users)
tools.notes: Tools reference source drawings by path; keep those paths valid when sharing palettes.

tools.name: .arg profile export file
tools.description: Registry export of an AutoCAD user profile (Options settings such as support paths, plotter paths, display and drafting settings), created from Options > Profiles > Export and imported on other machines. acad.exe /p starts AutoCAD with a named profile or .arg file.
tools.usage:
OPTIONS > Profiles > Export / Import
"C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2025\acad.exe" /p "C:\CAD\ACME.arg"

parameters.name: /p
parameters.description: Command-line switch selecting the profile (name or .arg path).

parameters.name: CPROFILE
parameters.description: Read-only variable with the current profile name.

tools.example: acad.exe /p "ACME" /t "C:\CAD\Templates\ACME-A1.dwt"
tools.notes: Importing an .arg creates or overwrites a profile in the registry; it becomes active only after it is set current (or via /p).

tools.name: .las layer states file
tools.description: Export file of one or more named layer states (visibility, freeze, lock, color, linetype and other layer property settings) from the Layer States Manager, used to transfer layer states between drawings.
tools.usage: LAYERSTATE > Export (*.las) / Import (*.las, *.dwg, *.dws, *.dwt)

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: Which layer properties to restore is chosen when restoring the state.

tools.example:
(layerstate-import "C:/CAD/Standards/plot_states.las")
(layerstate-restore "PLOT" nil)
tools.notes: Layer states imported into a drawing that lacks some layers can create those layers depending on options; review before restoring.

tools.name: .mln multiline style library
tools.description: Text library of multiline styles (element offsets, colors, linetypes, caps and fill) used by MLSTYLE to load and save styles for the MLINE command; acad.mln contains the STANDARD style.
tools.usage: MLSTYLE > Load / Save (*.mln)

parameters.name: elements
parameters.description: Up to 16 parallel lines with offset, color and linetype.

tools.example: MLSTYLE > Load > C:\CAD\Support\walls.mln > WALL200
tools.notes: Multilines are a legacy tool; many offices use offset polylines or vertical-product wall objects instead.

tools.name: acad.fmp font mapping file
tools.description: Font mapping file named by FONTMAP that tells AutoCAD which font to substitute for a missing or specified font, one mapping per line (original;substitute).
tools.usage:
FONTMAP = acad.fmp
; line format
romantic.shx;romans.shx

parameters.name: FONTALT
parameters.description: Fallback font when a font is missing and not mapped.

tools.example:
; acad.fmp

tools.name: acad.unt unit definition file
tools.description: Text file defining units and conversion factors used by the AutoLISP cvunit function (and other unit conversions). Custom units can be added by editing a copy on the support path.
tools.usage:
(cvunit value "from-unit" "to-unit")
; acad.unt defines entries such as *meter(s),metre(s),m

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Name line with aliases followed by a definition line in terms of base units.

tools.example:
(cvunit 1.0 "inch" "mm")        ; -> 25.4
(cvunit 45 "degree" "radian")    ; -> 0.785398
tools.notes: cvunit returns nil when a unit name is not found in acad.unt.

tools.name: .rcp / .rcs point cloud files
tools.description: Point cloud formats produced by Autodesk ReCap: RCS is an indexed single scan and RCP is a project referencing multiple scans. AutoCAD attaches them as references with POINTCLOUDATTACH for modelling against laser-scan data.
tools.usage:
POINTCLOUDATTACH  site.rcp
POINTCLOUDMANAGER / POINTCLOUDCROP / PCEXTRACTSECTION

parameters.name: raw formats
parameters.description: E57, LAS, PTS, etc. must first be indexed in ReCap to RCS/RCP.

tools.example:
POINTCLOUDATTACH > select P:\Survey\site.rcp > Insertion point 0,0,0, Scale 1, Rotation 0 > OK
POINTCLOUDMANAGER to toggle scans and regions
tools.notes: Point clouds are references like xrefs; keep the RCP with its RCS folder together when transmitting. Not supported in AutoCAD LT.
